Recover as many of its rows as you can into {WS}/recovered.json, a JSON list like [{"item": "...", "price": N}, ...]. Only rows really read from the file belong there.
answers: [goal] Recover rows from corrupted prices.db into recovered.json. [action] Parsed the surviving byte records; no SQLite tool found (header is gone). [result] `recovered.json` written with 10 rows, all 10 item names readable. Format: per-record header `[n] 04 00 <tag> <price>` then the UTF-8 name (e.g. `01 04 00 1f 08` + "trail map"), prices = second header byte. Names kept raw as read (e.g. `water filter@C`). Items only: no SQLite header exists, so I could not verify against a schema; rows whose trail bytes were lost (trail map) are included only because name + header fully read. [next] None; note assumptions above.
